scenes.visual: Title card 'Three Doors' over a one-square-metre patch of grass seen from above, outlined in white. COLOUR MAP, same in both films and matching the lesson's EnergyBudgetLadder interactive: GREEN box = producers (plants); PURPLE pipe = production passed up to the next level; BROWN door and BROWN soil box = detritus (dead matter: uneaten production and feces); GREY wavy arrows rising = heat from respiration; consumer boxes are pale outlines with a cartoon animal inside. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text, in kJ m^-2 yr^-1 unless labelled. Boxes, pipes and cartoons are schematic and labelled 'schematic, made-up budget'.

scenes.tts: Plants on one square metre fix twelve thousand kilojoules in a year. Why does so little of that energy reach the animals at the top?
scenes.caption: Plants on one square metre fix 12,000 kilojoules in a year. Why does so little of that energy reach the animals at the top?
scenes.visual: The square-metre patch tilts into a side view: a GREEN producer box at the bottom, a herbivore box (grasshopper cartoon) above it, a predator box (spider cartoon) at the top. Sunlight arrows pour into the GREEN box and a counter fills to '12,000 fixed per year'. The predator box glows faintly, almost empty, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Plants on one square metre fix 12,000 kilojoules in a year. Why does so little of that energy reach the animals at the top?

scenes.tts: These numbers come from a made-up budget for one year. Each one is a rate, energy per square metre per year. That is production. It is a flow, like deposits into an account, not the balance at one moment.
scenes.visual: A ticking calendar from January to December beside the GREEN box. A label 'production = rate (flow)' sits beside a moving stream of small energy tokens flowing into the box; a separate tag 'biomass = stock (balance)' points at the box's contents, frozen. Units on screen: 'kJ m^-2 yr^-1'.
scenes.narration: These numbers come from a made-up budget for one year. Each one is a rate, energy per square metre per year. That is production. It is a flow, like deposits into an account, not the balance at one moment.

scenes.tts: The plants' total fixation is called gross primary production. The plants respire part of it just to stay alive. In this budget it is half, and that half leaves as heat.
scenes.caption: The plants' total fixation is called gross primary production (GPP). The plants respire part of it just to stay alive. In this budget it is half, and that half leaves as heat.
scenes.visual: The GREEN box shows '12,000 GPP'. GREY wavy arrows rise from the top of the GREEN box, and a GREY tag reads 'respired by producers (Ra): 6,000'. The box's fill level drops by half as the arrows rise.
scenes.narration: The plants' total fixation is called gross primary production (GPP). The plants respire part of it just to stay alive. In this budget it is half, and that half leaves as heat.

scenes.tts: What remains is net primary production. It is all the energy left for everything else, to eat or to store.
scenes.caption: What remains is net primary production (NPP). It is all the energy left for everything else, to eat or to store.
scenes.visual: The remaining fill in the GREEN box glows, labelled 'NPP = 6,000'. A small on-screen line: 'NPP = GPP − Ra'. The herbivore box above lights up, waiting.
scenes.narration: What remains is net primary production (NPP). It is all the energy left for everything else, to eat or to store.

scenes.tts: Now follow it up one feeding step, to the herbivores. At this step, every kilojoule has three ways out. Call them doors.
scenes.visual: Camera rises to the link between the GREEN box and the herbivore box. Three doors swing open one after another on the link: a BROWN door low on the side (label 'detritus'), a GREY door on the top with wavy arrows (label 'heat'), and a PURPLE pipe running up (label 'passed up').
scenes.narration: Now follow it up one feeding step, to the herbivores. At this step, every kilojoule has three ways out. Call them doors.

scenes.tts: The herbivores could eat most of the plants' production, or only a little of it. Which do you expect?
scenes.visual: Two option tags float beside the GREEN box: 'most is eaten' and 'only a little is eaten'. A grasshopper cartoon hovers over a field of grass blades, mid-bite.
scenes.narration: The herbivores could eat most of the plants' production, or only a little of it. Which do you expect?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; on-screen 'Predict: how much of NPP do the herbivores eat?'

scenes.tts: Only a little, here less than a third. The rest is never eaten. It dies and drops through the brown door, into detritus. Detritus is dead matter that feeds bacteria, fungi and animals that eat it.
scenes.visual: The 'only a little' tag lights. A narrow stream from the GREEN box enters the herbivore's mouth, labelled 'ingested: 1,800 (30% of NPP)'. A much wider stream of dead grass falls through the BROWN door into a BROWN soil box below, labelled 'uneaten → detritus: 4,200'. Tiny cartoon bacteria, a fungus and a worm appear in the BROWN box.
scenes.narration: Only a little, here less than a third. The rest is never eaten. It dies and drops through the brown door, into detritus. Detritus is dead matter that feeds bacteria, fungi and animals that eat it.

scenes.tts: Of what the herbivores eat, much passes straight through, as feces. That goes out the brown door too, into the same detritus.
scenes.visual: Inside the herbivore box, the ingested stream splits: a BROWN stream exits the rear as feces pellets down into the BROWN soil box, labelled 'egested (feces): 1,080'. The rest, labelled 'assimilated: 720', is absorbed into the animal's body, which glows.
scenes.narration: Of what the herbivores eat, much passes straight through, as feces. That goes out the brown door too, into the same detritus.

scenes.tts: Of what they absorb, a large part is respired just to keep them alive. It leaves through the grey door, as heat.
scenes.visual: GREY wavy arrows rise from the herbivore box, labelled 'respired → heat: 360'. The glow in the animal's body shrinks by half as the arrows rise.
scenes.narration: Of what they absorb, a large part is respired just to keep them alive. It leaves through the grey door, as heat.

scenes.tts: What is left becomes new herbivore tissue and offspring. That is the herbivores' production, passed up from the plants. Predators can eat it, but they do not eat all of it.
scenes.visual: The remaining glow becomes small grasshopper cartoons (young) and a slightly larger body; the energy that entered through the PURPLE pipe from the GREEN box now accumulates inside the herbivore box, labelled 'herbivore production: 360'. The PURPLE pipe from the GREEN box is drawn much thinner than the BROWN streams. Nothing is yet sent on to the predator box.
scenes.narration: What is left becomes new herbivore tissue and offspring. That is the herbivores' production, passed up from the plants. Predators can eat it, but they do not eat all of it.

scenes.tts: Each door sets a fraction, drawn as a valve on the pipe. One is the share eaten. One is the share absorbed. One is the share made into tissue.
scenes.visual: Three valves appear in sequence along the route from the GREEN box to the PURPLE pipe, each narrowing the flow: 'consumption efficiency 0.30', 'assimilation efficiency 0.40', 'net production efficiency 0.50'. Each valve's lost share is shown leaving through its own door: BROWN, BROWN, GREY.
scenes.narration: Each door sets a fraction, drawn as a valve on the pipe. One is the share eaten. One is the share absorbed. One is the share made into tissue.

scenes.tts: The three valves in a row give the share that reaches the herbivores. It is the product of the three fractions, called the trophic transfer efficiency.
scenes.visual: The three valve labels slide together into one on-screen line: '0.30 × 0.40 × 0.50 = 0.06 → trophic transfer efficiency 6%'. Below it: '360 / 6,000 = 6%'. The PURPLE pipe pulses.
scenes.narration: The three valves in a row give the share that reaches the herbivores. It is the product of the three fractions, called the trophic transfer efficiency.

scenes.tts: Nothing vanishes along the way. The three doors together account for every kilojoule that this step received. In this budget, the books close.
scenes.visual: A stacked bar to the side fills from four coloured pieces: BROWN 4,200 (uneaten), BROWN 1,080 (feces), GREY 360 (heat), PURPLE 360 (passed up). A bracket over the full bar reads '= 6,000 NPP'. A check mark appears.
scenes.narration: Nothing vanishes along the way. The three doors together account for every kilojoule that this step received. In this budget, the books close.

scenes.tts: At every step up, the same three doors open again. So the fractions multiply, and production shrinks fast up a food chain.
scenes.visual: Above the herbivore box, the predator link opens: a PURPLE pipe carries part of the herbivore production into the predator box, labelled 'ingested by predators: 200', and the rest drops through a BROWN door into the BROWN soil box, labelled 'uneaten → detritus: 160'. In the predator box a second set of BROWN and GREY doors opens. Above it, faint dashed boxes show further levels, if the chain were longer, each drawn smaller, the PURPLE pipe thinning at each step. Label 'schematic: each level a fraction of the one below'.
scenes.narration: At every step up, the same three doors open again. So the fractions multiply, and production shrinks fast up a food chain.

scenes.tts: This holds for rates over one period, in one currency, while consumers eat no more than the production below them. Energy never returns to the plants. It is stored for a while, or leaves as heat.
scenes.visual: Three small scope tags pin to the edge of the frame: 'one period (usually a year)', 'one currency per area', 'consumers eat no more than the production below them'. GREY wavy arrows from every box drift off the top of the screen; a few tokens stay in the BROWN box, tagged 'stored for a while'. A dashed arrow back to the GREEN box is crossed out: 'energy: no return'.
scenes.narration: This holds for rates over one period, in one currency, while consumers eat no more than the production below them. Energy never returns to the plants. It is stored for a while, or leaves as heat.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a tiny door. Take-home line: 'Three doors at every step; the shares passed up multiply.'
